title: Stop Renting Your Cognitive Infrastructure - Thiyagarajan Maruthavanan, Kalmantic Labs
talk_summary: A founder describes inference costs ballooning (a stolen key, agent-loop waste, a $200M retailer anecdote) and argues that post-PMF teams should stop renting inference and build/own their own serving infrastructure. The actionable content is mostly at the layer of token/context cost control and workload-aware serving, not agent orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Input-token compression and context hygiene in agent loops
takeaways.what_they_do: Treats wasteful per-call input tokens and repeated agent-loop calls as the primary cost driver, and compresses/trims inputs before sending rather than only managing context window size.
takeaways.evidence_quote: many people forget about doing compression of their input token. And when there are agent loops, then there are many of these calls that are happening which are very, very wasteful

takeaways.technique: Hard spend caps and key-rotation on inference credentials
takeaways.what_they_do: After a leaked API key drained spend from $7k toward $10k, they arrested it with monitoring and a hard cap; the lesson is per-key budgets and anomaly alerts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: my key got stolen... I could see the cost rise up from 7,000 to 7,500 dollars to 8,000
takeaways.numbers: cost arrested at $10,000 instead of potentially $100,000

takeaways.technique: Workload-shape-aware routing instead of one endpoint for all calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Argues the inference endpoint is blind to workload shape, so cost blows up; routing/serving should match the shape of each call (short vs long, batch vs interactive).
takeaways.evidence_quote: The inference endpoint that is consuming this is is completely unaware of the shape of the workload

takeaways.technique: Own vs rent decision by maturity stage
takeaways.what_they_do: Frames build-vs-rent as a stage decision: rent while pre-PMF, own once usage is predictable and rate limits/control matter.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you want to learn, you can rent, but if you want to earn, then you have to own
